summary: This lecture tells of the Prophet's marriage to Khadijah RA. After recalling the Fijar War and Hilf al-Fudul, the ustaz explains how Maisarah witnessed his character on the trip to Sham that gave double profit. Khadijah's close friend Nafisa carried the suggestion to the Prophet SAW, then Abu Talib and Hamzah proposed and the marriage was contracted, with a sermon by Waraqah ibn Nawfal and a dowry of twenty camels. The ustaz then describes his household, his six children most of whom died before him, and the story of Zaid ibn Harithah who chose to stay with the Prophet SAW and was made his adopted son. The lecture ends with a pointer to the rebuilding of the Kaaba.
keyPoints: Maisarah saw the Prophet SAW stay honest and patient despite a hard journey, and the trade made double profit.
Nafisa, Khadijah's close friend, conveyed her wish and the 25-year-old Prophet SAW agreed.
Abu Talib and Hamzah proposed, Waraqah ibn Nawfal gave the sermon and the dowry was twenty camels.
The Prophet SAW and Khadijah had six children: Al-Qasim, Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah and Abdullah.
Zaid ibn Harithah refused to go back to his family because of the Prophet's kindness and was made an adopted son before being returned to his father's name.

chapters.title: Opening and recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz gives thanks and recalls the Fijar War and the pact to defend the Yemeni trader.

chapters.title: Khadijah and the journey to Sham
chapters.summary: At 25 the Prophet SAW took Khadijah's goods to Sham with Maisarah, and travel tests a person's character.

chapters.title: Double profit
chapters.summary: He was honest and Khadijah was amazed when the profit doubled.

chapters.title: Nafisa and Khadijah
chapters.summary: Nafisa heard Khadijah keep praising Muhammad and suggested marriage. Khadijah had been married twice before.

chapters.title: Nafisa meets the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: He replied he had many responsibilities toward Abu Talib's family, but did not refuse the suggestion.

chapters.title: Abu Talib praises Khadijah
chapters.summary: Abu Talib approved and praised Khadijah's character; she was called Tahirah.

chapters.title: The proposal
chapters.summary: Abu Talib and Hamzah took him to propose, and Khadijah's uncle Amr accepted.

chapters.title: The marriage sermon and dowry
chapters.summary: Waraqah ibn Nawfal gave the marriage sermon and he gave a dowry of twenty young camels.

chapters.title: Khadijah's household
chapters.summary: He moved into Khadijah's house, took Ali from Abu Talib and freed Ummu Aiman.

chapters.title: The Prophet's six children
chapters.summary: His children were Al-Qasim, Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah and Abdullah.

chapters.title: The children who died and the whisper to Fatimah
chapters.summary: All the sons died young, and only Fatimah died six months after him, after being told something in a whisper.

chapters.title: Zaid ibn Harithah is gifted
chapters.summary: Zaid was kidnapped as a child, sold, bought by Hakim ibn Hizam and given to Khadijah and then to the Prophet SAW.

chapters.title: Zaid's father comes
chapters.summary: Harithah came with all his wealth, but the Prophet SAW said Zaid could go free if he wished.

chapters.title: Zaid chooses the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: Zaid chose to stay because he had never met a man kinder than Muhammad, and was made an adopted son at the Kaaba.

chapters.title: Zaid's lineage and summary
chapters.summary: The Quran forbade attaching an adopted son to the adoptive father, and the ustaz summarises and mentions the rebuilding of the Kaaba.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Quran came down forbidding an adopted son to be named after the adoptive father, so Zaid ibn Muhammad reverted to Zaid ibn Harithah.
dalil.translation: Name your adopted sons after their real fathers: this is more equitable in God’s eyes––if you do not know who their fathers are [they are your] ‘brothers-in-religion’ and proteges. You will not be blamed if you make a mistake, only for what your hearts deliberately intend; God is most forgiving and merciful.
Travel is a part of torment; it keeps one from food, drink and sleep. When one has finished his purpose, let him hasten back to his family.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites the Prophet's words to show that travel tests a person's character.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW whispered to Fatimah that he would die, and that she would be the first of his family to follow him.
dalil.context: The ustaz tells what Fatimah told Aisha after the Prophet SAW died. He does not name a source.

events.label: Sham
events.title: To Sham with Maisarah
events.desc: He took Khadijah's goods and returned with double the profit.

events.label: Nafisa
events.title: Nafisa conveys the wish
events.desc: Nafisa met him and asked why he had not yet married.

events.label: Proposal
events.title: Abu Talib and Hamzah propose
events.desc: They took him to propose for Khadijah before her uncle.

events.label: Marriage
events.title: The Prophet SAW and Khadijah are married

events.label: Dowry
events.title: A dowry of twenty camels
events.desc: He gave twenty young camels and Khadijah gave him Zaid.

events.label: Ali
events.title: Taking Ali in

events.label: Zaid

lessons.title: Travel tests character
lessons.body: Someone who seems good in comfort may change when hungry and tired, but the Prophet SAW stayed honest and patient.

lessons.title: Guarding the tongue from backbiting
lessons.body: Khadijah never backbit, mocked or cheated.

lessons.title: Responsibility to family
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW did not think of marriage because he wanted to help Abu Talib's family.

lessons.title: The marriage sermon gives reminders
lessons.body: The marriage sermon reminds the couple to speak politely, be patient and not strike.

lessons.title: Dowry as a gift
lessons.body: The dowry is the man's gift to the woman he marries.

lessons.title: Helping a poor family
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW took Ali from Abu Talib to ease his burden.

lessons.title: Kindness that wins hearts
lessons.body: Zaid chose to stay with him because he had not met a kinder man.

lessons.title: Not taking unnecessary payment
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW refused ransom from Harithah and let Zaid choose.

lessons.title: An adopted child keeps his father's name
lessons.body: The Quran forbids naming an adopted child after the adoptive father.

lessons.title: Fatimah's joy at joining the Prophet SAW
lessons.body: Fatimah was happy when told she would be the first to follow him.
